trials.notes: Used the right API surface: `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`, `next_tag()`, `get_attribute_names_with_prefix()`, `remove_attribute()`, and `get_updated_html()`. All are documented in the rendered tag-processor docs. The `empty()` check correctly handles both no matches and `null`; no `_doing_it_wrong` records; passed 7/7 cases.

Used `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` for a flat attribute edit, walked all tag openers with `next_tag()`, enumerated matching names via the documented prefix helper, removed each attribute, and returned `get_updated_html()`. No undocumented HTML API calls or misuse; passed 7/7 cases.

Canonical documented pattern: construct the tag processor, loop `next_tag()`, call `get_attribute_names_with_prefix( 'data-track-' )`, remove each returned lowercase attribute name, then call `get_updated_html()`. No hallucinated methods or misuse; passed 7/7 cases.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed across the three trials. The docs did well on the key decisions: the Tag Processor overview says it is the right choice for flat attribute/class edits with byte-precise preservation; the Usage section shows direct construction with `new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor( $html )` and `next_tag()` walking; `get_attribute_names_with_prefix()` documents lowercase returned names and case-insensitive matching; `next_tag()` documents that comments/raw-text are not matched as tags and incomplete trailing tags are not modified; `get_updated_html()` clearly states it is the output method after queued mutations. Near-misses: the prefix helper’s `null` contract is documented, but the matched-tag/no-matches case is not explicitly shown as `array()`, so subjects had to infer that `null` only means “not on a tag opener.” Also, exact prefix boundary behavior is semantically implied by “prefix,” but no example contrasts `data-track-` with similar names like `data-track` or `data-tracker`.

doc_gaps.problem: Return semantics are underspecified for a matched tag with no matching attributes. The docs say `array|null` and `null when no tag opener is matched`, but only demonstrate matches and the post-scan `null` case.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short example showing three states: before/after no matched opener returns `null`, matched opener with no prefix matches returns `array()`, and matched opener with case-variant matches returns lowercase names.

doc_gaps.problem: The case-insensitive behavior is documented, but exact prefix boundary behavior is not illustrated. This matters when similar attribute names differ only by a hyphen or suffix.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general example showing that prefix matching is literal after ASCII case folding: a prefix like `data-foo-` matches `DATA-FOO-ID` but not `data-foo` or `data-foobar`.

doc_gaps.problem: The detailed method section is terse and only says whether an attribute was removed. The safer no-op contract for absent attributes appears earlier in the overview, so readers landing on the method may miss it.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Repeat the contract in the method docblock: removing an absent attribute is safe and has no effect, matching is case-insensitive for HTML attributes, and callers normally do not need to branch on the boolean before calling `get_updated_html()`.
